title: Centralized customer request routing + priority ladder for top-account escalations
creator: Riya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Top-account product requests and escalations are inconsistent across CSMs/AE/Support. We receive duplicated asks via email, Slack, Intercom, and ad-hoc calls; the product team lacks a single source of truth to triage, prioritise, and commit roadmap items tied to commercial impact. This causes delayed decisions, missed SLAs for strategic customers, and poor signal into planning cycles.

Objective: Create a repeatable intake & prioritization flow that routes top-account requests into a product triage board, scores requests by business impact and technical effort, and enforces clear SLAs (time-to-triage, decision windows). Deliver a pilot with 3 strategic accounts and instrument metrics for OKR alignment.
proposed_solution: 1) Create a lightweight Top-Account Intake form (Confluence + Google Form initially, then a Zendesk/Intercom webhook) capturing: account, ARR influence, customer blocker severity, reproducibility, regulatory/compliance risk, workaround, and suggested priority.

2) Develop a priority ladder algorithm (scorecard) with weighted factors: Revenue impact (40%), Outage/blocker (25%), Strategic dependency (15%), Frequency (10%), Legal/regulatory risk (10%). Produce scoring spreadsheet + sample thresholds for P0/P1/P2.

3) Implement routing automation: form -> Zendesk ticket with tags -> Linear triage board + Slack channel (#top-account-triage). Use a webhook to create structured Linear issues with labels and attachments (PRD template link).

4) Triage cadence & RACI: Weekly product triage (PM, Eng lead, Solutions Eng, CSM owner) to make decision: Accept into a short-term scoped work, Defer to backlog, or Escalate to Exec review. Establish 48h SLA for initial triage on P0/P1 items.

5) Pilot + feedback loop: Pilot with three accounts for six weeks. Capture qualitative feedback (CSMs/AE), and iterate score weights and thresholds. Build a lightweight dashboard (Looker/Metabase) for metrics.
6) Bake into roadmap planning: Force link accepted requests to initiatives/OKRs and surface in cycle planning docs so commercial impacts are visible to prioritization conversations.
acceptance_criteria: Top-Account Intake form created and published to CSMs/AEs with guidance doc
Automation exists: form submissions create Linear issues with standardized fields and tags
Priority ladder scorecard documented and applied to pilot submissions
Weekly triage meeting scheduled with invites to PM/Eng/SE/CSM and a published RACI
Pilot onboarded with 3 accounts and at least 6 submissions processed
Dashboard tracks: time-to-triage, time-to-decision, percent decisions met within SLA, and % of accepted items linked to an OKR or initiative
Working PRD template linked on created issues and one full PRD produced for an accepted pilot item
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize intake fields and priority weights (this ticket)
Week 1: Build form + automation prototype (CSM-run Google Form + Zapier -> Zendesk -> Linear) and publish to pilot CSMs
Week 2-7: Pilot with 3 accounts; run weekly triage and collect feedback
Week 8: Analyze pilot metrics, adjust scorecard thresholds, and finalize automation for org-wide rollout
Week 9-10: Documentation, training for CSM/AE, and enablement in internal playbooks
Post-rollout: Integrate into roadmap cadence and include metric in PM OKRs
metrics: Primary: Median time-to-triage (target: <= 48 hours for P0/P1)
Primary: Percent of triage decisions met within SLA (target: >= 90% after pilot)
Secondary: Percent of accepted items linked to roadmap initiatives/OKRs
Secondary: Mean time from acceptance to shipped or prioritized backlog (baseline during pilot)
Customer metric: NPS change among pilot accounts for product responsiveness
Operational: # of duplicate requests reduced (baseline vs pilot)
Business: ARR at-risk events reduced for pilot accounts
